notes: εἰς τὸ … ἐσθίειν is analysed as rule 61 requires: the governing preposition takes the clause-introducing to and the nominalizing article is unrepresented, which is the same analysis the contract gives the spelled-out to the end that (rule 24).
The single English who covers the substantival article before ἔχοντα under rule 90, a lone relativizer being pronoun and relativizer at once; the participle keeps its own verb.

τις → a man heads on man because the only other word in the unit is a supplied determiner, which rule 17 forbids as a head; 8:2 and 8:3 head their any man on any because the ASV wrote a different English word there, so the English differs rather than the analysis.
εἰδωλείῳ → an idol's temple heads on temple, the noun that glosses the compound lexeme (rule 66), and κατακείμενον → sitting at meat heads on the verb word that glosses the lexeme (rule 91).
οὐχί carries content of its own and is aligned to not in the ordinary way; rule 64's unrepresented arm is for a particle whose only work is to mark the question.
